ops.title: promotions review: two path-resolution semantics, never unify
ops.body: Adversarial review of the capt-hook promotions wave (2026-07-19) caught a security regression before ship: ScratchPath was switched to util.paths.resolve_target (parent-resolved, final component literal) — correct for DELETION targets (classify the symlink itself) but wrong for WRITE-APPROVAL (must follow the final symlink to the true destination), letting a scratch-located symlink to a real file get writes auto-approved under skip-permissions. Fix: ScratchPath fully resolves (conditions.py docstring names the boundary); resolve_target stays parent-only for command targets; Target.path in the upcoming cmd.py documents the asymmetry. Three minors also fixed pre-ship: bootstrap cooldown persisted before spawn (spawn outside the locked mutate block), atomic_write pinned to UTF-8, binary_supports errors=replace. Lesson: path-resolution helpers encode a THREAT MODEL, not just path math — promotion must match per-consumer semantics, and finder+refuter both independently found this via concrete symlink repros.
